I was thinking about Fitting's theorem (#39813) (in fact, because I decided that it was too easy a problem for lean-eval, but still not in Mathlib).

I wanted to use (lowerCentralSeries ↥S n).map S.subtype, i.e. the lower central series of a subgroup, viewed back in the ambient group. This felt cumbersome, and I'd like to propose adding it as Subgroup.lowerCentralSeries, with dot notation:

def Subgroup.lowerCentralSeries (S : Subgroup G) : ℕ → Subgroup G
  | 0 => S
  | n + 1 => ⁅Subgroup.lowerCentralSeries S n, S⁆

So S.lowerCentralSeries n : Subgroup G. The existing lowerCentralSeries G n is the case S = ⊤.

  • Proofs that need to bound LCS terms of H relative to other subgroups of G are forced into .map H.subtype plumbing. The current proof in the Fitting PR hides the concept behind (fun X => ⁅X, S⁆)^[n] S because I didn't want to commit to new API without discussion, but it's ugly.
  • You could tidy a few things already in Nilpotent.lean:
    • lowerCentralSeries_map_subtype_le: (lowerCentralSeries H n).map H.subtype ≤ lowerCentralSeries G n becomes H.lowerCentralSeries n ≤ lowerCentralSeries G n.
    • Subgroup.isNilpotent and nilpotencyClass_le each lose ~3 lines of simp only [SetLike.le_def, mem_map, exists_imp] plumbing.
  • The same .map subtype friction will show up in future work towards CFSG, I think: Brauer-Suzuki, Glauberman ZJ, signalizer functors: anywhere we want to talk abut the lower central series of multiple subgroups at once.

I think it's relatively inexpensive to provide the api and glue for a new definition, but I'm happy not to if people think the existing machinery suffices.

Prior context: #Is there code for X? > Fitting subgroup and Frattini subgroup of a finite group back in October.
@Damiano Testa and I had the same opinion about adding Subgroup.lowerCentralSeries (and perhaps even letting it replace the existing def?)
Indeed, I also have a formalisation of this result and I would have liked to have the various "series" be subgroup-valued.

Great. #39844 is now a preliminary PR that generalizes Subgroup.lowerCentralSeries to take a subgroup as an argument. It looks pretty pleasant I think.

My preference is to leave the relativization of derivedSeries to a separate PR. (Relativing upperCentralSeries isn't particularly straightforward, so I definitely want to leave that out of scope.)

The Fitting's theorem PR at #39813 is now stacked on top, the diff is https://github.com/kim-em/mathlib4/compare/feat/subgroup-series...feat/fitting-theorem, and better than it looked before this refactor.
